transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-09-29T10:00:00Z
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Amir Hassan (Redwood CSM), Ethan Morales (Cypress Dynamics - Head of MLOps), Priya Singh (Platform Eng), Daniel Cho (CTO)

SUMMARY:
Weekly pilot bench digest to reconcile latency/throughput numbers vs their incumbent provider, triage routing decisions and decide whether to request dedicated slots for next sprint. Focus on p95 latency, sustained throughput, token costs, and fallbacks.

TOPICS:
- Baseline vs Redwood latency/throughput numbers
- Quantization tradeoffs and quality checks
- Routing policy for mixed workloads (low-latency vs high-throughput)
- Dedicated slots request and cost implications
- Compliance items: SOC2, KMS, SSO

TRANSCRIPT:
00:00 Jordan Lee: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, yeah it's 10am on our side, uh quick roll call? (laughs)
00:07 Ethan Morales: Ethan here, priya, daniel too, hi
00:10 Priya Singh: Priya on platform
00:12 Daniel Cho: Daniel, thanks
00:15 Maya Patel: Maya from infra, hey
00:18 Jordan Lee: cool, i'll kick off with the headline numbers then maya will walk through the lab runs, so short story: across the daytime workload you shared, we see median token latency about 48ms, p95 132ms on the redwood profile. baseline vendor p95 was ~210ms in our runs, so sizeable delta. throughput sustained at 420 req/s with our batching config whereas baseline stalled around 180 req/s under the same concurrency mix.
00:45 Ethan Morales: wow 420, that's a big jump. are those numbers for the long form generation or short prompts?
00:50 Jordan Lee: mixed — this run was our mixed-profiles test, 40% short prompts, 60% 512 token-ish generation, we used sequence-length distribution you provided, maya?
00:59 Maya Patel: yeah so we replayed the traffic trace you sent, there was a 512 ceiling for the big requests, we enabled continuous batching with a 6ms window and prefix KV catch, uh K-V catch, sorry — kv cache — was warm for about 65% of requests which helped p50 more than p95. there's some jitter on p95 tied to cold kv misses.
01:22 Priya Singh: when you say "kv catch" (laughing) i'm like what is that — ok got it
01:26 Jordan Lee: spellings aside (laughs). the other piece is quantized model variant we used — int4 mixed — so cost per token in the lab was about $0.0024 equivalent for generation compare vs baseline quoted $0.0045, gives you a nice delta on unit economics.
01:44 Daniel Cho: did we see any quality regression with the int4 run? that's a big concern for us
01:49 Maya Patel: we ran the eval set you shared and A/B'd outputs, measured rouge/semantic sim on around 500 examples; average similarity dropped about 0.8% absolute on the quantized path, mostly on very specific factual prompts. we flagged 12 examples where hallucination rate increased slightly. we can push a slightly higher precision for that workload slice.
02:11 Ethan Morales: okay that's reasonable, maybe we only quantize the high throughput routes
02:15 Jordan Lee: exactly that's the routing idea. the routing policy proposal — Maya has a slide — is to route latency-sensitive short interactions to the unquantized variant pinned to dedicated slots, and route batch/high-throughput long gens to the quantized pooled nodes.
02:31 Maya Patel: right, so two lanes: lane A low-latency, no-quantize, reserved capacity; lane B high-throughput quantized, pooled autoscale. with the traffic mix you gave, lane B would consume about 60% of tokens but lane A needs tight p95 SLA under 150ms.
02:48 Priya Singh: that SLA target is the ask from customer ops, yes
02:51 Jordan Lee: then the question becomes do you want Reserved slots or Dedicated capacity for lane A? reserved gives predictable latency but costs more. we modelled monthly committed commit showing cost delta of about 23% vs pure hosted with burst.
03:08 Daniel Cho: do we have exact numbers? engineers want to see the CSV
03:11 Jordan Lee: yes i'll send the per-route latency CSV, that will include median, mean, p95, p99, and token counts per route. action item on me.
03:22 Ethan Morales: thanks.
03:24 Maya Patel: a couple of other notes from lab: we saw two notable tail cases — one due to cold kv misses (we recommend pre-warming on top routes) and one due to occasional model checkpoint swaps when we hit autoscale events. the autoscale thresholds we used were conservative; increasing slot concurrency reduces p95 but can increase variance, so we landed on concurrency 12 per GPU for lane B.
03:50 Jordan Lee: can you repeat the swap detail — is that an infra flapping event?
03:54 Maya Patel: it's not flapping, it's more like model load/unload during scale-up. if a spike comes in and we fire up a new pod, that pod loads a checkpoint which can add 600-900ms for the first request; most subsequent requests are fine. that's why we recommend warm standbys or keepalive slots for lane A.
04:14 Ethan Morales: hmm that aligns with our infra constraints — we don't want 800ms spikes on checkout flows
04:19 Jordan Lee: undestandable. we can keep 2 hot standbys for lane A to eliminate that class of tail. cost tradeoff is predictable; we'll model it in the spreadsheet.
04:28 Priya Singh: on security: we're tracking SOC2 and KMS — amir (from redwood) had a note?
04:33 Amir Hassan: yes i pinged earlier, we have SOC2 type 2, we can share redacted reports; for KMS we integrate with AWS KMS and HSM via our private deployment connectors, we've done customer integrations with SAML, SSO, role-based access controls, logging to your SIEM. i'll drop the docs link.
04:50 Daniel Cho: any extra work to get KMS configured for Private? we need to know if HSM support requires on-prem or can be cloud KMS
04:57 Amir Hassan: can be both, cloud KMS is typical; HSM is available for VPC/private installs, we have a runbook.
05:05 Jordan Lee: ok circling back to the comparative numbers — baseline vendor had a p95 of ~210ms, we have 132ms. Token cost delta roughly 40-50% depending on quantization. throughput is 420 vs 180 under the same concurrency mix. caveat: these are lab runs, not production traffic yet.
05:28 Ethan Morales: what about warmup time to reach 420? did you need sustained ramp or was it immediate?
05:33 Maya Patel: ramped over ~90 seconds with autoscaler; sustained 420 for a 10 minute window under test harness. peak spikes hit 480 briefly before queueing.
05:42 Priya Singh: ok good.
05:44 Jordan Lee: another item is fallbacks — if lane B gets overloaded we degrade to a slightly smaller model to keep throughput but tradeoff quality. we can configure automatic fallback thresholds at 95% CPU or queue length. that was a requirement you'll mentioned earlier, e.g., graceful degradation.
06:00 Ethan Morales: yes, graceful degrade is must-have. but we have to validate the smaller model doesn't break our downstream parsers
06:06 Maya Patel: agree, so we suggest a canary where 1% flows hit fallback in staging to validate parsing before we enable auto-fallback in prod.
06:15 Daniel Cho: timeline: if we accept routing config and dedicated slots, how soon can we get a production-like run?
06:20 Jordan Lee: if you share the production sample traffic by EOD Friday, we can mirror a prod-like replay next week. the dedicated slots approval adds a procurement step — Amir can coordinate.
06:31 Amir Hassan: i'll own the procurement thread, help with quote and docs.
06:34 Priya Singh: for the procurement we also need the expected monthly committed tokens and a SLO addendum
06:40 Jordan Lee: we'll include committed tokens estimates in the quote, and an SLO addendum template.
06:45 Maya Patel: quick note on quality regression monitoring — we integrated a regression alert that flags any drift in semantic-similarity below a threshold tied to your eval set; we can wire that to slack or pager.
06:58 Ethan Morales: how noisy is that metric? we don't want false alarms.
07:02 Maya Patel: we tune it to group around 24-hour rolling window and require a 2-sigma drop before opening an alert, then it surfaces sample diff outputs.
07:12 Priya Singh: ok, useful.
07:15 Jordan Lee: let's go over the risks and mitigations quick: risk 1 cold kv misses -> mitigation pre-warm top routes; risk 2 autoscale load/unload adds tail -> mitigation warm standbys; risk 3 quantization quality delta -> mitigation route-sensitive quantization and staged eval; risk 4 procurement delay -> mitigation temporary hosted burst capacity while procurement finishes.
07:44 Ethan Morales: makes sense.
07:47 Daniel Cho: what about regional failover? if eu region has outage what's the failover plan?
07:52 Maya Patel: we can route to another region but latency will be higher, and for low-latency lane A we keep active-active only if you want the extra cost; otherwise active-passive is default.
08:03 Priya Singh: we need cross-region data residency checks too
08:06 Amir Hassan: noted, we'll provide the compliance note.
08:09 Jordan Lee: ok action items — i'll recap then we'll hand to amir for docs and pricing. jordan will send CSV, maya will send quantization notes, amir SOC2 and KMS docs, ethan will drop prod traffic sample.
08:24 Ethan Morales: yes i'll upload today.
08:27 Jordan Lee: next steps in calendar: propose a slot-approval meeting w/ your infra and procurement next tuesday, 2026-10-06; does that work?
08:36 Daniel Cho: i can do tuesday
08:38 Priya Singh: yep
08:40 Jordan Lee: great, we'll send invite. thanks all
